messages:
Aisha Khan: quick heads-up — ACME pilot asked to lift the EU softcap on priority lane burst for first 30 days. They want guaranteed burst during launch window. Need guidance for packaging + contract language. :eyes:
Ben Lee: do we have their expected qps/spike profile? lift vs temporary addon changes cost a lot.
Aisha Khan: they sent this: peak 6M tokens over 10 mins, baseline 200k tokens/min otherwise. expecting 2 week ramp.
Sam Ortiz: if numbers are accurate we should avoid a free permanent carveout. options: 1) time-limited burst addon (pay per-burst) 2) reserved capacity + discounted burst 3) canary with strict budget cap + auto-throttle.
Ben Lee: agree. preferred default: burst addon with hard cap and auto-fallback to lower-tier model when cap hit. keeps routing simple.
Marta (Legal): from contract side we need clear language on territory and SLA impact. if we promise 'guaranteed burst' across EU we may need infra commitments and data residency clauses. also export/regulatory check.
Aisha Khan: understood. customer is sensitive to any throttling during demo. they want seamless experience for pilot.
Sam Ortiz: launch criteria suggestion: (a) validated spike tests on staging (b) billing shape agreed (c) fallback model & cadence tested (d) incident playbook + escalation path.
Ben Lee: operationally we can deliver a 30-day "Pilot Burst Pack": one-time purchase that attaches to account, has X tokens of burst, consumed first, price = reserved premium. After pack exhaustion, fall back to normal quota.
Aisha Khan: can we make X configurable per-customer? ACME wants 6M tokens/increase.
Ben Lee: yes but need to map to GPU capacity. For 6M tokens in 10 min that's N GPUs at p95 latency target. We can offer a size S/M/L pack with explicit throughput guarantees.
Marta (Legal): draft clause suggestion (example):
"Pilot Burst Pack": Customer may purchase a one-time Pilot Burst Pack specifying burst capacity and duration. Redwood provides best-effort allocation; in the event of critical capacity constraints Redwood will (i) notify Customer, (ii) provide fallback options, and (iii) credit Customer for unmet service.
Marta (Legal): this avoids absolute "guarantee" wording while giving remediation path.
R&D Bot: quick infra note: workable approach is to route burst requests to dedicated priority pool flagged by account_id, with per-pool autoscale policy and quota token consumption. sample config:
priority_pools:
  - name: pilot-burst
    burst_quota_tokens: 6000000
    duration_secs: 2592000 # 30 days
    fallback_model: rwd-gpt-medium
Ben Lee: two product tradeoffs: (1) pricing math for burst (one-off prepaid vs usage overage) (2) complexity in rollout UI + billing. we should aim for simplest that legal signs off.
Aisha Khan: next steps: Ben to draft pricing bands + UI callouts, Sam to list launch/test criteria, Marta to iterate contract wording, I'll sync with AE and get customer's precise spike window.
Sam Ortiz: I'll add the test checklist to the pilot playbook and estimate runbook time.
Ben Lee: I'll mock price points: S=2M tokens @ $X, M=6M @ $Y, L=12M @ $Z and share in thread.
Marta (Legal): also flag: any cross-border data flow during pilot? if yes, we need DPA amendment or region-specific hosting.
Aisha Khan: noted. thanks everyone, will update after AE sync. :thumbsup:
